Answer any FIVE questions. All questions carry 20 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Study the following Gannt Chart for a project and then answer the questions that follow:

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2022-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_7_fig_1.png)

(i) Define the term 'critical path' in project management. (2 marks)

(ii) Determine the critical path of the above project. (3 marks)

(iii) Define the term 'slack time' of a task. (2 marks)

(iv) Identify activities in the project that have slack time and calculate their respective duration in days? (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reading the chart.** Each column is one day and the bar of an activity covers the days it takes:

| Activity | Days (columns) | Duration | Starts after |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1 to 3 | 3 days | - |
| B | 4 to 5 | 2 days | A |
| C | 4 to 7 | 4 days | A |
| D | 6 to 8 | 3 days | B |
| E | 9 to 10 | 2 days | D |
| F | 8 to 11 | 4 days | C |

The project therefore has two paths from the start to the end: $A \to B \to D \to E$ and $A \to C \to F$.

**(i) Critical path (2 marks).** The critical path is the **longest sequence of dependent activities** from the start to the end of the project. It gives the shortest possible time in which the whole project can be completed. Its activities have no slack time: a delay in any of them delays the whole project.

**(ii) Critical path of the project (3 marks).** The duration of each path is:

- $A \to B \to D \to E$: $3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10$ days;
- $A \to C \to F$: $3 + 4 + 4 = 11$ days.

The longest path is $A \to C \to F$, so the **critical path is A - C - F**, and the project takes **11 days**.

**(iii) Slack time (2 marks).** The slack time (or float) of a task is the **length of time by which the task can be delayed (or lengthened) without delaying the end of the whole project**. It is the difference between the latest and the earliest start of the task (it is zero for activities of the critical path).

**(iv) Activities with slack time (4 marks).** The activities that are not on the critical path are **B, D and E**, which form the path $A \to B \to D \to E$ of 10 days. Since the project lasts 11 days:

$$\text{slack} = 11 - 10 = 1 \text{ day}$$

| Activity | Duration | Earliest start (after day) | Latest start (after day) | Slack |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B | 2 days | 3 | 4 | 1 day |
| D | 3 days | 5 | 6 | 1 day |
| E | 2 days | 8 | 9 | 1 day |

Each of B, D and E can be delayed by one day without delaying the project (but this one day is shared by the three activities: if B uses it, D and E can no longer be delayed). The activities A, C and F have a slack of 0 days.

(The durations of the activities with slack are B = 2 days, D = 3 days and E = 2 days.)

**(i) Three health hazards (6 marks, 2 marks each)**

1. **Back and neck pain (poor posture).** An operator sitting for long hours on a chair that cannot be adjusted to his or her height cannot keep the back straight and the feet flat, so the back, neck and shoulders become painful and the posture may be damaged.
2. **Eye strain and headaches.** Poor lighting (some bulbs not lit) makes the operator strain to read the screen and the keyboard, which causes tired, watery eyes, headaches and a loss of sight in the long term.
3. **Repetitive strain injury (RSI) of the fingers, hands and wrists.** Pressing hard on keys repeatedly for long periods injures the tendons and nerves of the fingers, wrists and arms (pain, numbness, carpal tunnel syndrome).

**(ii) Advice to the company (3 marks, 1 mark each)**

1. Buy **adjustable ergonomic chairs** with back support, and place the screen at eye level, so that the operator sits with a straight back and the feet on the floor.
2. **Replace the faulty bulbs** and provide enough, even lighting (also use anti-glare screens, avoid light shining on the screen) and have the operators' eyesight checked regularly.
3. **Repair or replace the stiff keyboard** (use a good keyboard and a wrist rest), teach the operators to type lightly, and let them take **short breaks** regularly to stand up, stretch and rest their eyes and hands.
